newsitem.title: CANADA: Thousands evacuated as Canada Peace River floods.
newsitem.headline: Thousands evacuated as Canada Peace River floods.

text.p: Four thousand people evacuated their homes in this northwest Alberta community of 7,000 Saturday as the Peace River flooded the region.

Peace River's town council declared a state of emergency at 9:30 a.m. after an ice jam on the river caused it to rise quickly and the Heart River to overflow its banks, according to the Canadian Press.
Peace River is 300 miles (485 km) northwest of Edmonton.
The Peace River level was the highest since 1935, though the ice jam later broke and the river began flowing freely, it said.
Most houses were not damaged but residents were evacuated as a precaution. Some residents were allowed to return late Saturday but the evacuation order remained in place for the downtown area.
The ice jam broke at about 12 noon EDT a little more than an hour after the river peaked, a town spokeswoman said.
There were no reports of injuries or any damage estimates.
On Saturday, provincial officials urged downstream residents to avoid the Peace River and move property and livestock to high ground.
